step "new migration timestamp versions"
git fetch --quiet origin main || printf 'preflight: could not fetch origin/main; using the local ref\n' >&2
base=origin/main
if git rev-parse --verify --quiet "$base" >/dev/null; then
  version_of() {
    name=${1##*/}
    printf '%s\n' "${name%%_*}"
  }
  main_migrations=$(git ls-tree -r --name-only "$base" "$migrations_dir/")
  for path in "$migrations_dir"/*.sql; do
    git cat-file -e "$base:$path" 2>/dev/null && continue
    version=$(version_of "$path")
    if ! printf '%s\n' "$version" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]{14}$'; then
      fail "$path is a new migration; use a 14-digit goose timestamp version (goose create without -s)"
      continue
    fi
    if ! awk -v version="$version" 'BEGIN {
      year = substr(version, 1, 4) + 0
      month = substr(version, 5, 2) + 0
      day = substr(version, 7, 2) + 0
      hour = substr(version, 9, 2) + 0
      minute = substr(version, 11, 2) + 0
      second = substr(version, 13, 2) + 0
      days[1] = 31; days[2] = 28; days[3] = 31; days[4] = 30
      days[5] = 31; days[6] = 30; days[7] = 31; days[8] = 31
      days[9] = 30; days[10] = 31; days[11] = 30; days[12] = 31
      if (year % 400 == 0 || year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) days[2] = 29
      valid = year > 0 && month >= 1 && month <= 12 && day >= 1 && day <= days[month] && hour <= 23 && minute <= 59 && second <= 59
      exit !valid
    }'; then
      fail "$path has an invalid goose timestamp version"
      continue
    fi
    other=$(printf '%s\n' "$main_migrations" | awk -F/ -v v="$version" '{ name = $NF; sub(/_.*/, "", name); if (name == v) print $0 }')
    if [ -n "$other" ]; then
      fail "$path reuses timestamp version $version of $other on $base; create a new timestamped migration"
    fi
  done
else
  fail "$base not found; cannot check migration numbers"
fi

29: func validateNewMigrationVersion(name string) error {
30: 	prefix, _, ok := strings.Cut(name, "_")

33: 	}
34: 	if len(prefix) != 14 {

38: 		return fmt.Errorf("invalid goose timestamp version: %w", err)
39: 	}

41: }

48:       fail "$path is a new migration; use a 14-digit goose timestamp version (goose create without -s)"
49:       continue
50:     fi
51:     if ! awk -v version="$version" 'BEGIN {
52:       year = substr(version, 1, 4) + 0
53:       month = substr(version, 5, 2) + 0
54:       day = substr(version, 7, 2) + 0
55:       hour = substr(version, 9, 2) + 0
56:       minute = substr(version, 11, 2) + 0
57:       second = substr(version, 13, 2) + 0

59:       days[5] = 31; days[6] = 30; days[7] = 31; days[8] = 31
60:       days[9] = 30; days[10] = 31; days[11] = 30; days[12] = 31
61:       if (year % 400 == 0 || year % 4 == 0 && year % 100 != 0) days[2] = 29
62:       valid = year > 0 && month >= 1 && month <= 12 && day >= 1 && day <= days[month] && hour <= 23 && minute <= 59 && second <= 59
63:       exit !valid
64:     }'; then
65:       fail "$path has an invalid goose timestamp version"
66:       continue
67:     fi
68:     other=$(printf '%s\n' "$main_migrations" | awk -F/ -v v="$version" '{ name = $NF; sub(/_.*/, "", name); if (name == v) print $0 }')
69:     if [ -n "$other" ]; then
70:       fail "$path reuses timestamp version $version of $other on $base; create a new timestamped migration"
71:     fi
72:   done
73: else
74:   fail "$base not found; cannot check migration numbers"
75: fi

78:   exit 1
79: fi
